memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"If the whole Israelite community sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the LORD's commands, even though the community is unaware of the matter, when they realise their guilt and the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the tent of meeting."'" - Lev 4:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God addresses something we rarely think about: sin that belongs to a whole group.

A community can drift together. A church can develop a culture of gossip, or a family can share a habit of dishonesty, or a workplace can normalise something everyone knows is wrong. Nobody planned it. Everyone participates. And the phrase God uses is striking: even though the community is unaware of the matter.

That is the danger of shared sin. It becomes invisible precisely because everyone is doing it. There is nobody left to notice.

Then comes the turning point: when they realise their guilt. God's mercy includes the moment of waking up. And when they wake, they do not each go their own way. The assembly brings one offering. They own it together.

Daniel prayed this way, confessing "we have sinned and done wrong" though he personally had been faithful (Dan 9:5). Nehemiah did the same. Isaiah, seeing God's holiness, said, "I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips" (Isa 6:5).

Sometimes the most honest prayer is not "forgive me" but "forgive us."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a sin I have accepted simply because everyone around me accepts it?
2. What would it look like for me to confess on behalf of my family, church, or community?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, open our eyes to what we have grown blind to together. Forgive us, and make us a people who see clearly again. Amen.
